Kenosha Public Market is a year-round Saturday market located in the heart of the Downtown district. Our vendors present a variety of products including local produce, artisan pastries and confections, locally sourced meats, poultry and eggs, fine cheeses, prepared foods & handmade gifts. Order from our online store, KPM2GO, to ensure you get the products you want before they sell out. Place orders during the week and pick up at our Saturday market!

Our location is in the center of this pedestrian-friendly neighborhood with convenient parking options, world-class museums, an authentic streetcar system, two lighthouses, unique dining, and plenty of shopping options. Kenosha Public Market is proud to be one of the many shopping destinations Downtown.

All of our farmers and artisans live within 60 miles of Chapel Hill, NC and bring fresh quality produce, value-added farm products, and crafts to market year-round.

The market is vendor run and operated by our market manager. Every dollar spent goes directly to our farmers and vendors. All items are grown, fished, or created by our farmers and artisans.

organization.description:
The GSFM is unique collaboration between local organizations with a shared goal of creating conditions under which people can be healthy. It is one of few markets in downtown Louisville and is dedicated to increasing availability of fresh foods to an underserved area. The market offers customers a great variety of local vendors and products. We are open the first Thursday of each month from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. from June through October.

HISTORY: In 2009, the University of Louisville School of Public Health and Information Sciences (SPHIS) led efforts to establish the Gray Street Farmers Market (GSFM) in partnership with the Louisville Metro Dept. of Public Health and Wellness (LMPHW). The GSFM operated weekly (rain or shine) from mid-May through the end of October for 11 seasons. We did not open in 2019 or 2020 due to COVID-19 pandemic and resource limitations .

organization.description:
Cuyahoga Valley Farmers Markets’ (CVFM) works to provide access to and education about sustainable foods and agriculture to the communities in Northeast Ohio by building connections between our community with the producers of locally grown food.
CVFM was established in 2022 to continue the operation of the long-running Countryside farmers markets in Howe Meadow and at Old Trail School, both located in the Cuyahoga Valley National Park. These vibrant farmers markets have been in operation since 2004 and have been growing steadily since their inception.
CVFM MARKET IMPACT:
During our Summer market in Howe Meadow (May-October) we connect on average 2,500 (peak 3,000) members of our community to producers of local food.
During our Winter market at Old Trail School (November-April) we have on average 600 shoppers per market (peak 1,000).
Provide consistent sales outlet for 70 local farms and businesses.

organization.description: Common Ground Producers and Growers is a mobile farmers market and food hub. It is a family-run agricultural organization based in Wichita, Kansas, operating the state’s longest-running Mobile farmers market and food hub. Founded in 2014 by multi-generational farmer and CEO Donna Pearson McClish, the organization was established to eliminate food insecurity by delivering fresh, locally grown produce directly into neighborhoods with limited access to healthy food. Guided by the motto “All are fed. No one is hungry.” Common Ground operates on Pearson’s Family Farms—the largest Black-owned urban farm in the region. On the farm, Common Ground aggregates, processes, and distributes Kansas-grown fruits and vegetables sourced from more than 40 farmers statewide. The mobile farmers market and food hub currently serves 37 locations across 10 cities and 4 counties, while ensuring equitable compensation for farmers and maintaining affordable prices for customers.

organization.description:
Nestled on the shady lawn of Plainfield’s historic Quaker church—one of the town’s founding buildings with over 175 years of history—our farmers market offers a truly unique and welcoming community experience. With more than 80 vendors each week, including a diverse lineup of local farmers, growers, bakers, and artisans, visitors can explore an abundant selection of fresh produce, vibrant flowers, handcrafted goods, and delicious homemade treats.

Our market also features around a dozen food trucks, offering a wide variety of freshly prepared meals and flavors. Guests can enjoy live music while they shop, along with weekly themes and family-friendly activities that make each visit special.

More than just a place to shop, our market is a celebration of local talent, agriculture, and community—an opportunity to support small businesses while enjoying the charm, history, and hospitality that make Plainfield unique.

organization.description:
The Chewelah Farmers Market is a non-profit and is run entirely by volunteers. The market is known for its vendor-friendly policies. Many of our vendors will tell you that this is their favorite market!
And our monthly special event days have garnered a following all of their own. Where else can you race a zucchini down the creek or shoot cherries at a target with a slingshot?
The Chewelah Farmers Market was selected by the Washington State Farmers’ Market Association as the Best Small Farmers’ Market in the state for 2010 and 2011. The mission is to make available high-quality, locally produced food and to promote self-sufficiency in the community food systems by providing a venue for local farmers, growers and producers to connect directly with consumers and to support educational opportunities.
We invite you to come on down to the beautiful Chewelah City Park on Fridays, mid-May through mid-October, and enjoy all that the Chewelah Farmers Market has to offer.

The AFM is a producer’s market. We maintain a strict focus on food and farms, showcasing locally grown, sourced, and produced foods. All products, both food and non-food, must be produced by the vendor. No re-selling is allowed.

organization.description:
Rowdy Stickhorse Farmers Market is the heart of local food in Northwest Oklahoma—a place where community, quality, and tradition come together every Saturday, rain or shine. Open May through September, from Memorial Day to Labor Day, our market proudly supports local farmers, ranchers, bakers, and makers by giving them a direct connection to the people they serve.

As the only certified farmers market in Northwest Oklahoma, we’re more than just a place to shop—we’re a gathering place built on relationships. At Rowdy Stickhorse, you’ll meet the hands that raised your beef, gathered your eggs, baked your bread, and crafted your goods. Every purchase supports hardworking local producers and keeps dollars right here in our community.

Our market is packed with fresh, local goodness. You’ll find locally raised meats, farm-fresh eggs, handcrafted and artisan breads, and an abundance of seasonal produce—ripe tomatoes, crisp cucumbers, sweet corn, and juicy watermelons straight from the field.

organization.description:
Mattapan Square Farmers Market
Our 20th season runs from July 11, 2026, to October 31, 2026, every Saturday from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM at the Corner of Cummins Highway and Fairway. The market runs from July to October and typically sees 200-400 shoppers per week. It is not only a place to purchase healthy food, but also serves as a place to bring residents together and as a resource for health education and other social issues.

The approach to our market is to ensure its accessibility to low-income families and to make sure the food sold is culturally relevant. We do this through selecting farmers that are able to sell their produce at reasonable prices, encouraging and facilitating the use of SNAP and HIP benefits, outreaching to WIC recipients who receive WIC farmers’ market coupons, and outreaching to elders who receive Senior Farmers Market coupons.
The Mattapan Square Farmers Market follows a safety protocol to ensure a safe and healthy opening and shopping experience!

Yes, leashed dogs are welcome! Please keep pets away from vendor booths and clean up after them.
Yes. The market runs along a flat, paved pathway from Beethoven Street to the carousel area. Some vendor booths are on grass, but the main route is accessible.

You’ll find fresh produce, baked goods, meats, dairy, prepared foods, plants, and locally made artisan products depending on the season. Vendors are primarily local farmers, food producers, and small businesses from the region.
